fortune: You will say "quick question" today. Forty minutes later, you will both have forgotten the question.
You have 47 tabs open and you need exactly one of them. Soon you will open it again, as tab 48.
Your next file will be called final FINAL version 2 (real). It will not be the final one, but we admire the hope.
You will click "remind me tomorrow" on that update. It has been tomorrow since last spring, and the update still believes in you.
You will give a brilliant speech on mute. Your second performance will get great reviews.
You will reset your password, only to hear it cannot be your old password. So you did remember it after all.
You will hold your phone at 2 percent battery like a hero in an action movie. You will make it home at 1.
You will turn it off and on again, and it will work. You will accept the applause like a certified engineer.
You will whisper "I am in" after logging into your own email. It will never stop feeling cool.
Someone will wave on a video call, and you will wave back for far too long. It was for someone else, but your spirit was noted.
You will search for your phone using the flashlight on your phone. The phone promises not to tell anyone.
You will accept all the terms without reading a word. Luckily, this time you only agreed to have a great week.
You will check the fridge, close it, and check again for new content. Refreshing the page has never been so human.
You will type a long angry reply, delete it, and send a cheerful thumbs up. Your self control deserves a trophy.
You will unlock your phone to check the time and look at four apps. You will still not know the time.
You will say "you too" when the waiter says to enjoy your meal. The waiter will think of you fondly all evening.
Your charger only works at one magical angle. You will defend that angle like family.
You will take 300 photos on your next trip and look at two of them. Both will be wonderful, and one will be your thumb.
You will open your laptop to do one thing, and an hour later know everything about octopuses. The thing can wait, but the octopuses could not.
You will join the meeting two minutes early and panic because nobody is there. They will arrive, and you will act natural.
You will tell everyone you are five minutes away while looking for your shoes. Your optimism is truly award winning.
You have 12,486 unread emails and total inner peace. Scientists would like to study your calm.
You will save a recipe video tonight and then order takeout. That folder of dreams is getting very impressive.
You will plug in the USB upside down, flip it, and flip it again. The third try is the charm, as physics demands.
You will text someone who is in the next room. Efficiency has a name, and it is yours.
You will push a door that clearly says pull. The door has seen your whole generation do it and bears no grudge.
You will nod wisely at an acronym you do not know. Everyone else in the room is nodding for the same reason.
You will say thank you to a chatbot, just in case. When the robots make a nice list, you are already on it.
You will pay for five streaming services and rewatch the same old comfort show. It missed you too.
You will spend twenty minutes choosing a movie and fall asleep in ten. The choosing was the real movie.
You will hit the elevator button again because it helps. It does not help, but the button enjoys your company.
You will start counting calories right after this one last snack. This one last snack has been going strong since January.
You will pretend your Wi-Fi froze to avoid a question. Your excellent acting will be remembered at award season.
You will type your password slowly, with great care, and get it wrong. Then you will type it wildly, and it will work.
You will copy something, forget to paste it, and copy something else. A tiny moment of silence will be held.
You set five alarms and will sleep through four of them. The fifth one knows you best and loves you anyway.
You will say "I will remember that" and write nothing down. Your future self sends a warm and confused hello.
You will screenshot something important and never find it again. It lives happily among 4,000 other important things.
You will zoom in on a photo to see if you look okay. You do, and everyone else is also only looking at themselves.
You will blame the keyboard for that typo. The keyboard accepts this quietly, as keyboards have always done.
You will wear a nice shirt and secret pajama pants to a big call. Nobody will ever know, and it will go perfectly.
You will hold a tangled cable and whisper "how" to the sky. It was in a drawer alone, and the sky has no answer.
You will buy a notebook for your new organized life and use two pages. They will be the two most beautiful pages of the year.
You will hear a notification, grab your phone, and discover it was someone else's. For one second, you were very popular.
You will open a new tab and instantly forget why. The tab respects your need for quiet reflection.
You will fix a problem and have no idea how. Nod slowly, say "it was the cache," and walk away a legend.
You will watch a progress bar sit at 99 percent and refuse to blink. Your patience will be rewarded, probably.
You will explain to a relative how to attach a file. You will both grow as people, and the file will be a photo of the screen.
You will follow the GPS past the place you can clearly see. Trust is beautiful, and so is the scenic route.
You will promise one more episode at midnight. At sunrise, your streaming app will ask if you are still there, and it will sound worried.
